title: IWE query language
description: The YAML query language of `iwe find`, `iwe count`, `iwe update` and `iwe delete`, as documented by `iwe docs query`. The parser stays the authority: this schema publishes the vocabulary and catches shape mistakes before an operation runs. The operation kind comes from the subcommand, not from the document, so the root is a union of the four kinds — point at `#/$defs/findOperation`, `#/$defs/countOperation`, `#/$defs/updateOperation` or `#/$defs/deleteOperation` when the kind is known, at `#/$defs/filter` for a `--filter` argument, and at `#/$defs/blockPredicate` for a block-operator argument. Seven rules the parser enforces and this schema cannot express: regex compilation (`$matches`, `pattern`); a `$within` mapping argument must select content (`{}`, or a predicate carrying `$section` / `$quote` / `$list`); `minDepth` must not exceed `maxDepth`, `minDistance` must not exceed `maxDistance`, and `expect.min` must not exceed `expect.max`; `$set` and `$unset` paths must not duplicate or prefix one another; `-k KEY` must not be combined with a `--filter` carrying `$key`; an integer is written as one — `1.0` and `1e3` fail the parser but are integers to JSON Schema, and every count fits a signed 64-bit integer; and the checks that happen at evaluation time (type compatibility, `$replaceText` anchors, disjointness, `expect` counts). The schema is stricter in one place: an explicit YAML null on an optional key (`sort: null`, `match: null`, `lexical: null`), which the parser reads as the key being absent, and an empty document are rejected here — write the key or leave it out.

operation.description: An operation document of any of the four kinds.

findOperation.description: `iwe find` — returns the matched documents, shaped by the projection.

countOperation.description: `iwe count` — returns the number of matched documents.

updateOperation.description: `iwe update` — mutates frontmatter and blocks on each matched document; the filter is required, so operating on the whole corpus means passing `{}` on purpose.

deleteOperation.description: `iwe delete` — removes each matched document and cleans up references; the filter is required.

filter.description: A filter document: `$`-prefixed keys are operators, bare keys are frontmatter field paths, and every top-level key is ANDed together. `$not` is not a document-level operator — use `$nor` for document-level negation.

filterList.description: A non-empty list of filter documents, the argument of `$and`, `$or` and `$nor`.

fieldValue.description: The value of a bare field key: a scalar or list is bare equality (a scalar tests membership in an array field), a mapping of `$`-keys is an operator expression, and a mapping of bare keys addresses nested fields. Mixing `$`-keys and bare keys in one mapping is an error.

fieldOperators.description: An operator expression on one field; operators in one expression are ANDed together.

$eq.description: Equal to the value; cross-type comparisons are always false.

$gte.description: Greater than or equal to the value.

$lte.description: Less than or equal to the value.

$in.description: Equal to any value in the list.

$nin.description: Equal to no value in the list.

$all.description: An array field containing every value in the list.

$type.description: The field's YAML type, or any of a list of types.

$size.description: The array field's length, as a count predicate.

$not.description: Negation of a field-level operator expression.

nestedFields.description: A mapping of nested field names, equivalent to the dotted path shorthand.

typeName.description: A YAML type name, as a quoted string.

countPredicate.description: A count test: a non-negative integer is an `$eq` shorthand, a mapping of comparisons ANDs them together.

keyOperator.description: `$key` — document identity. A scalar is the key itself; the mapping form carries exactly one of `$eq`, `$ne`, `$in`, `$nin`.

inclusionAnchor.description: The argument of `$includes` / `$includedBy`: a scalar key is the direct-edge shorthand; the mapping form takes an optional `match`, inclusion-walk bounds and an optional `$size`. Omitting `maxDepth` means direct edges; `maxDepth: 0` is the unbounded sentinel.

match.description: The anchor set, as a filter; defaults to any document.

maxDepth.description: Upper bound of the inclusion walk; `0` is unbounded.

minDepth.description: Lower bound of the inclusion walk.

$size.description: Test the count of related documents instead of mere existence.

referenceAnchor.description: The argument of `$references` / `$referencedBy`: a scalar key is the direct-edge shorthand; the mapping form takes an optional `match`, reference-walk bounds and an optional `$size`. Omitting `maxDistance` means direct edges; `maxDistance: 0` is the unbounded sentinel.

match.description: The anchor set, as a filter; defaults to any document.

maxDistance.description: Upper bound of the reference walk; `0` is unbounded.

minDistance.description: Lower bound of the reference walk.

$size.description: Test the count of related documents instead of mere existence.

blockOperators.description: The block-operator vocabulary, shared by block predicates, the `$matches` projection source and the block update operators. Text predicates match a block's own text only, never descendant text.

$text.description: Own text contains the string, case-insensitively; `{ $eq: S }` matches the whole own text.

$matches.description: Own text matches the Rust regex, case-sensitively unless the pattern carries an inline `(?i)` flag.

$within.description: Blocks inside the selection, at any depth; a scalar names a section, and a mapping argument must select content.

$contains.description: Blocks with a descendant matching the predicate, at any depth.

$section.description: A header together with everything below it; a scalar is exact-text shorthand for the root header.

$header.description: Heading lines alone, no implicit subtree; a scalar is exact-text shorthand.

$paragraph.description: Paragraphs; a scalar is exact-text shorthand.

$item.description: List items, excluding nested children; a scalar is exact-text shorthand.

$code.description: Fenced code blocks, excluding the fence lines; a scalar is exact-text shorthand.

$table.description: Tables, one line of own text per row; a scalar is exact-text shorthand.

$ref.description: Block references, selected by target; text predicates match the authored link text alone, and the scalar shorthand is an error.

$hr.description: Horizontal rules; no own text, so the scalar shorthand and direct text predicates are errors.

$quote.description: A block quote together with its contents; the root has no own text, so the scalar shorthand and direct text predicates are errors.

$list.description: A list together with its items; the root has no own text, so the scalar shorthand and direct text predicates are errors.

$references.description: Blocks whose own content links to the key.

$and.description: Every predicate in the list matches.

$or.description: Any predicate in the list matches.

$nor.description: No predicate in the list matches.

blockPredicate.description: A mapping of block operators; `{}` matches every block, top-level keys AND together, and bare keys are errors.

emptyHeadPredicate.description: A block predicate for a block with no own text: `$text` and `$matches` cannot apply directly — scope with `$within` or `$contains`.

matchesSource.description: The argument of the `$matches` projection source: a regex scalar, or a mapping combining the bare `pattern` payload with `$`-keys that scope it.

pattern.description: The Rust regex applied to the own text of every block in scope.

projection.description: `project` — a mapping of output names to sources, or a block predicate directly, which reads as the document's `key` plus a `content` field narrowed to the selection.

projectionFields.description: A mapping of output names to projection sources.

projectionSource.description: Where an output field's value comes from: `1`, `true` and YAML null take the frontmatter field of the same name, a dotted path takes a nested frontmatter field, a `$`-selector takes a system field, and the mapping forms read blocks.

anyOf.description: The body narrowed to the selected blocks, rendered at their original depth.
One entry per selected block: `type`, `path` and `text`.
Grep — one entry per matching line.

search.description: `find` only — full-text selection and default ordering; at least one ranker is required.

lexical.description: BM25 full-text query over title and body.

fuzzy.description: Subsequence query over title and key.

sort.description: Exactly one sort key: `1` ascending, `-1` descending. Ties break by document key ascending.

limit.description: The maximum number of documents; `0` means no limit.

expect.description: A guard on the number of applications: an exact count, or a range with `min` and/or `max`.

update.description: The mutations applied to each matched document; frontmatter operators and block operators combine freely and apply atomically per document.

$unset.description: Remove frontmatter fields; the values are ignored.

$replace.description: Replace each target with the `content` markdown.

$insertBefore.description: Insert the `content` markdown as a sibling before each target.

$insertAfter.description: Insert the `content` markdown as a sibling after each target.

$append.description: Append the `content` markdown as the last child of each target; containers only.

$replaceText.description: Rewrite the own text of every selected block, un-coalesced.

setFields.description: Field paths to values; a mapping value replaces wholesale, so write subset leaves with the dotted shorthand.

unsetFields.description: Field paths to remove; the values are ignored.

contentBlockUpdate.description: A block update carrying markdown: the `$`-keys select, the bare `content` is the payload, and `expect` guards the number of targets.

content.description: The markdown payload, parsed and normalized on write.

replaceTextUpdate.description: `$replaceText` — with `from`, that byte-exact substring of each selected block's own text becomes `to`; without it, `to` replaces the entire own text.

from.description: The substring to replace; must occur exactly once in each selected block's own text.

deleteBlockUpdate.description: `$delete` — the `$`-keys select and there is no payload; an argument with no `$`-keys selects every block.

fieldPath.description: A frontmatter field path: dot-separated segments, each non-empty, none starting with `$`, and none carrying whitespace or control characters.

outputName.description: A projection output name: one path segment — no `.`, no leading `$`, no whitespace or control characters.
